OsteosarcomaSurgery.title: Osteosarcoma Surgery
OsteosarcomaSurgery.SubTitle: Comprehensive Guide | InDocsCare Medical Services
OsteosarcomaSurgery.Intro: Explore the latest, patient-focused surgical treatments for osteosarcoma, including limb-sparing surgery and amputation. Learn how InDocsCare offers expert orthopedic oncology care for children and adults in India.
OsteosarcomaSurgery.WhatIsDescription: Surgery plays a<bold> critical role in the treatment of osteosarcoma</bold>, a type of aggressive bone cancer. Whether in children, teens, or adults, surgical procedures are aimed at:
OsteosarcomaSurgery.WhatIsPoints3: Preserving as much function and appearance of the limb as possible
OsteosarcomaSurgery.WhatIsNote: At <bold>InDocsCare,</bold> we collaborate with top orthopedic and oncology surgeons in India to deliver personalized, advanced surgical care for osteosarcoma patients from around the world.
OsteosarcomaSurgery.DiagnosisTitle: 🔬 Diagnosis First: The Importance of Biopsy
OsteosarcomaSurgery.DiagnosisDescription: Before any surgery, a <bold>biopsy</bold> is performed to confirm the diagnosis. This is not just a step—it’s a <bold>strategically critical action.</bold>
OsteosarcomaSurgery.DiagnosisNote: 🛑 Note: The biopsy and tumor removal surgery must be planned together by an experienced orthopedic oncologist to prevent complications or the need for more radical surgery. It is defer patient to patient a doctor can take decision accordingly.
OsteosarcomaSurgery.GoalTitle: 🎯 Goal of Surgery: Complete Tumor Removal
OsteosarcomaSurgery.GoalDescription: The<bold> primary surgical objective</bold> is a <bold>wide excision</bold>—removing the tumor with a margin of healthy tissue to ensure no cancer cells remain. This reduces the risk of recurrence or metastasis.
OsteosarcomaSurgery.GoalPoints1: Negative margins (no cancer at edges): Ideal outcome
OsteosarcomaSurgery.GoalPoints2: Positive margins (cancer at edges): May require additional treatment
OsteosarcomaSurgery.Type1Points2: Tumor removed while saving the limb
OsteosarcomaSurgery.Type1Points3: Internal prosthesis or bone graft used to replace excised bone
OsteosarcomaSurgery.Type1Points5: <bold>Note for Children:</bold> Advanced noninvasive expandable prostheses are available that grow with the child—reducing the need for repeated surgeries.
OsteosarcomaSurgery.Types2Points1: Considered when tumors are too large or involve critical blood vessels/nerves
OsteosarcomaSurgery.Types2Points2: Followed by prosthetic fitting and rehabilitation
OsteosarcomaSurgery.Types2Points3: Can be life-saving and functionally empowering when necessary
OsteosarcomaSurgery.ReconstructiveDes: In cases where traditional limb preservation isn't possible, our surgeons offer:
OsteosarcomaSurgery.ReconstructivePoints1: <bold>Rotationplasty: </bold>A functional reconstructive option often used in children
OsteosarcomaSurgery.ReconstructivePoints2: <bold>Joint Fusion:</bold> For stabilization when joint reconstruction isn't feasible
OsteosarcomaSurgery.ReconstructivePoints3: <bold>Bone Grafts + Magnetic Expandable Implants </bold>for growing children
OsteosarcomaSurgery.PediatricDescription: Children face unique challenges. InDocsCare ensures:
OsteosarcomaSurgery.PediatricPoints2: Multidisciplinary care with pediatric oncologists and rehabilitation experts
OsteosarcomaSurgery.PediatricPoints3: Emotional and psychological support for young patients and families
OsteosarcomaSurgery.PediatricQuote: ⭐ "Growth in young patients is vital. Our noninvasive expandable implants and limb-salvage procedures aim to preserve both function and future."
OsteosarcomaSurgery.RecoveryNote: With proper rehab, most patients regain excellent limb function and quality of life.
OsteosarcomaSurgery.MetastaticDescription: If the cancer has spread (commonly to the lungs), additional surgery may be recommended. InDocsCare offers:
OsteosarcomaSurgery.MetastaticPoints3: Careful assessment of lung nodules via CT scans and intraoperative evaluation

NonInvasiveExpandableProsthesis.hopeTitle: A New Hope for Children with Bone Cancer
NonInvasiveExpandableProsthesis.hopeDesc: Bone cancer in children, especially osteosarcoma, often affects growth plates in the limbs, posing a major challenge:<bold> how to remove tumors while preserving limb function and allowing normal growth.</bold>
NonInvasiveExpandableProsthesis.hopeDesc2: Traditionally, limb salvage surgery required multiple operations to lengthen the limb as the child grows. But today,<bold> noninvasive expandable prostheses</bold> are changing that reality—<bold>minimizing surgeries, pain, and recovery time</bold>.
NonInvasiveExpandableProsthesis.note: <bold> Note</bold>: Treatment outcomes can vary from patient to patient. Before making any decision, we highly recommend sending us your<bold> medical reports.</bold>
NonInvasiveExpandableProsthesis.teamDesc: 🩺 Our team will carefully review your case in consultation with top <bold>specialists and expert doctors</bold>, and provide you with a personalized treatment plan and cost estimate.
NonInvasiveExpandableProsthesis.whatIsTitle: What Is a Noninvasive Expandable Prosthesis?
NonInvasiveExpandableProsthesis.whatIsDesc: A non-invasive expandable prosthesis is a specially designed implant that can<bold> extend in length without the need for further surgery</bold>. Using magnetic or electromagnetic technology, the implant is gradually lengthened as the child grows, without anaesthesia or hospital stays.

NonInvasiveExpandableProsthesis.whatIsPoints1: Preserves the function and appearance of the limb
NonInvasiveExpandableProsthesis.whatIsPoints3: Ensures safety through advanced procedures and technologies

NonInvasiveExpandableProsthesis.boonDesc: For orthopedic and oncology surgeons, these prostheses offer<bold> predictable outcomes</bold>, lower complication risks, and greater patient satisfaction. They also allow for <bold>customized treatment plans</bold> based on the child’s age, growth rate, and tumour details….
